title: Warmup oscillation comparison: Llama / Mistral / Qwen
content:
Summary:

Quick notes from a set of empirical runs comparing warmup / throughput oscillation behavior across three model families (Llama family 2.1B baseline, Mistral 7B variant, Qwen 2B hybrid) under long-context workloads (2k, 8k, 32k). Goal: understand the transient oscillation pattern we see in production traces during sustained sessions and identify cheap mitigations that avoid degrading steady-state throughput.

High-level takeaway:
- All three families experience a warmup period, but the temporal dynamics differ: Llama converges fastest and shows smallest amplitude oscillation; Mistral exhibits large periodic dips (visible in p95 and throughput) correlated with asynchronous KV garbage/eviction activity; Qwen exhibits mid-sized oscillations, sensitive to PCIe DMA bursts on A100s with heavy multi-model mix.

Experiment setup (notes / commands):
- Hardware: A100-80GB (prod cluster), H100-80GB (dev comparison), 1-socket per worker.
- Serving runtime: rtx/1.5.2 (bench harness + continuous-batcher), with kv-cache enabled, default cache-reservoir 0.25, dynamic-batching on.
- Model bits: Llama-2.1B (fp16), Mistral-7B (fp16 + fused-kernel), Qwen-2B (int8 4-bit simq). No MoE variant here for Llama/Mistral/Qwen baseline; separate MoE runs below.
- Input patterns: 25 concurrent sessions each seeding the model with a 64-token priming prompt then streaming 2k / 8k / 32k continuation at 1 token/sec emulated arrival (to highlight long-lived context behavior).
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95 latency per-token, sustained throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization, GPU memory fragmentation (from nvprof and custom memmap), PCIe DMA counters, scheduler queue length, KV hit ratio.
- Trace capture: perf traces + serving runtime traces (trace ids: warmup-exp-20240918-{llama,mistral,qwen}).

Observed behavior (by model):
- Llama-2.1B:
  - Warmup period ~12–20s to reach steady-state throughput for 2k/8k. For 32k takes ~35s.
  - Oscillation amplitude small: 6–12% throughput variance (peak-to-trough) after warmup; p95 stable (+-8% around median).
  - GPU mem fragmentation low, KV hit ratio ramps to >95% within 25s.

- Mistral-7B:
  - Warmup longer: ~25–45s depending on context length.
  - Periodic throughput dips every ~18–28s once steady-state established (observed as ~20–30% reduction in tokens/sec lasting 2–4s).
  - Correlated signals: short-lived spike in cudaFree / allocator activity, sudden increase in page-fault-like stalls on the UVM path for A100 config.
  - KV hit ratio fluctuates: when dips occur, cache hit falls ~8–12% for 1–2s then recovers.
  - Hypothesis: fused kernels + background reclamation cause transient memory reclamation / defragmentation that blocks small allocations used in routing/prefetching path.

- Qwen-2B:
  - Warmup intermediate: ~18–30s.
  - Oscillation amplitude 12–18% with irregular period (no strict cadence; correlated with PCIe DMA bursts and kernel launch jitter).
  - On H100 runs, oscillation amplitude reduced ~30% vs A100, pointing to PCIe vs NVLink differences.

MoE-specific experiments (Mistral-MoE toy):
- Setup: Mistral-MoE 12-expert variant with gating configured to route 2 experts per token; same long-context workload as above.
- Observations:
  - MoE increases both warmup time and oscillation amplitude. Cold expert activation causes localized memory pressure on particular CUDA streams that cascades into router stall events.
  - When the routing distribution shifts (session drift), we observe a series of staggered micro-dips as new experts are touched for the first time; these micro-dips accumulate into a visible oscillation on p95.
  - Measured: expert-first-touch events correspond to 3–9% latency spike for subsequent tokens while kernel hotpaths synchronize.

Representative numbers (aggregated):
- 32k sessions, batch size 1 continuous:
  - Llama p95 steady: 92ms (std +-7ms), oscillation amplitude ~9%
  - Mistral p95 steady: 130ms (std +-18ms), periodic dips to 180–210ms (~30% worse)
  - Qwen p95 steady: 110ms (std +-12ms), sporadic peaks to 150ms
  - Mistral-MoE p95 steady: 170ms with bursts up to 260ms when new experts are activated

Trace excerpts / diagnostic signals seen in profiler (short snippets):
- timing window: 2024-09-18T14:03:22Z (mistral)
  - serving_runtime::router::route - 4.8ms -> spike to 42ms (during dip)
  - allocator::reclaim_loop - executed for 2500us repeatedly in the same 2s window
  - gpu_dma: pcie_rx_burst_count +12% coincident with kernel serialization

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Background allocator / defrag operations (tied to fused kernel memory patterns in Mistral) are co-scheduled with routing kernels causing short windows of serialization — primary cause of periodic dips in Mistral.
2) MoE first-touch expert activation causes localized pressure on particular CUDA streams and cross-stream synchronization penalties — amplifies any underlying allocator-induced jitter.
3) Qwen sensitivity arises from PCIe DMA bursts during cache eviction (int8 packing/unpacking) on A100; NVLink/H100 better hide these bursts.

Quick mitigation ideas tested (and results):
- Pinning and pre-alloc: pre-allocate biggest ephemeral buffers during model load and pin them to avoid allocator-driven defrag. Result: Mistral dips amplitude reduced by ~40% but memory footprint increases ~6%.
- Staggered expert warmup: prior to accepting live traffic, execute a lightweight pass to touch each expert buffer sequentially. Result: eliminated first-touch staircase events for MoE runs; overall warmup longer by ~8s but steady-state p95 improved by 10%.
- Soft-rate smoothing: throttle ingress token rate for the first 30s to allow KV priming. Result: trivial effect on oscillation amplitude for Mistral (allocator still fires), but helpful for Qwen by avoiding synchronized DMA peaks.
- Batch window smoothing (continuous-batcher parameter change): increase max-batch-window from 40ms -> 80ms to reduce scheduling churn; yields small reduction in p95 jitter for Llama and Qwen, negligible for Mistral.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Is allocator defrag triggered by a specific fused kernel or a sequence of allocations used only by the Mistral kernel path? Plan: capture allocator full stack traces during dip windows (nvprof+jemalloc stack capture).
- Re-run Mistral on H100 / NVLink to see if hardware interconnect changes behavior (we have a two-node dev H100 cluster).
- For MoE: test alternative gating (top-1 vs top-2) to measure how many expert touches cause sustained pressure.
- Investigate moving background reclaim into a lower-priority worker thread that yields to routing. Risk: may increase memory footprint if reclaim delayed.

Action items (short):
- [Aisha] schedule allocator stack trace capture during next mistral 32k run (ticket INF-1986).
- [Daniel] run warmup experiment on H100 node and share perf traces (due 2024-10-04).
- [Sofia] prototype staggered-expert-warmup hook in model loader (WIP PR branch warmup/stagger-expert).
- [Liam] simulate ingress soft-rate smoothing in load-test harness and measure impact on control-plane metrics.

Notes to self / rough heuristics:
- If p95 oscillation amplitude >20% and periodic: suspect allocator/defrag.
- If oscillation correlates with new sessions touching unseen experts: MoE-first-touch.
- If irregular spikes align with DMA counters: PCIe / eviction path.

Appendix: commands used (bench harness snippets)
- ./bench --model mistral-7b --context 32768 --sessions 25 --tokens-per-session 32000 --arrival-rate 1tps --collect-traces warmup-exp-20240918-mistral
- ./runtime-inspect memmap --pid $PID --period 100ms > mistral-memmap-09-18.log
- nvprof --profile-from-start off --trace-mem-alloc --log-file mistral-nvprof.log --pid $PID

End-of-note.

(Informal draft, rough numbers — use bench run artifacts for authoritative values.)
